findings.quote: The GFIP was an attempt to privatise a state function – for the benefit of the connected elite – and the resistance by millions of motorists marked a turning point in South African politics… the place where the ANC government of the time was told not to rip off its own people.
findings.steelman_for: The editorial is clearly marked as opinion and is arguing a policy case about e-tolls and the user-pays principle. The cabinet write-off itself is a public announcement, and the ANC's historical role in introducing Gauteng e-tolls is a matter of public record.
findings.steelman_against: Unattributed loaded language in the outlet's own voice (connected elite; rip off its own people) frames the ANC as predatory. The fetched body does not carry an ANC reply to those characterisations.
findings.evidence_notes: Quote Proven in the fetched body of the 9 June 2026 editorial (byline Editorial staff). Framing is the driver. The cabinet write-off is Established as a report of the announcement; the quoted moral and causal claims are Alleged.

findings.quote: Like old Donnie Trump across the sea, Zuma is an astute politician and a stubborn person who won’t let facts or public opinion make up his mind for him.
findings.steelman_for: This is a clearly labelled View of the Week column comparing two public political figures. Opinionated characterisation of a public official is expected in a signed column, and Zuma's public record is discussed elsewhere in the same piece.
findings.steelman_against: The column asserts, in the writer's own voice, that Zuma will not let facts or public opinion change his mind and (in the following lines) is obsessed with power and enrichment. The fetched body does not carry a response from Zuma. One finding is recorded on Zuma; a second finding on Trump is not added from the same simile.
findings.evidence_notes: Quote Proven in the fetched body (typographic apostrophe in won't). Framing is the driver. The character claims are Alleged.
